next_question: Can a bias-corrected conditional mutual information estimator (equal-weight PMI, median PMI, or direct CMI via KSG/KNN) recover stable, finite-sample-convergent measurements on the 12-state hash-routed SPA, and does the corrected estimator detect K3-K2 > 0.1 bits with valid null centering — or does the weighted-averaged PMI bias (0.41 bits asymptotic) mask a genuinely zero beyond-Markov signal?
why_next: This experiment demonstrates the weighted-averaged PMI estimator is asymptotically non-convergent (K2 grows from 0.933 at N=5000 to 1.779 at N=50000) with systematic positive bias ~0.41 bits (null mean 0.407, 4.07x threshold). The estimator fails identically across 5 frameworks (parametric bootstrap 0.357, Miller-Madow 0.407, conditional entropy -0.814, within-stratum 0.417, shuffled-action 0.407) confirming the bias is intrinsic to PMI weighted averaging across heterogeneous strata, not permutation scheme or estimator variant. The K3-K2 ratio test (designed to avoid null centering) also fails: bootstrap CI includes zero and bootstrap mean (-0.109) is not centered on observed (0.287), indicating K3 estimator fragility under session resampling. The Markov-vs-beyond-Markov question remains the highest-information open question for C-WEB-DYNAMICS but requires a convergent estimator before any PMI-based inference is valid. A bias-corrected estimator is the minimum prerequisite for continuing the PMI research program on this SPA class.

established: Weighted-averaged PMI estimator is asymptotically non-convergent: K2 PMI grows from 0.933 (N=5000) to 1.779 (N=50000, +84.5%). Bias is not finite-sample. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 result.json:metrics.exploratory_n50000)

Null control bias floor ~0.41 bits is intrinsic to weighted-averaged PMI across deterministic/stochastic strata (31.5% deterministic at N=5000, 2.6% at N=50000). Bias persists across 5 independent frameworks with range 0.357-0.417 bits. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit.json V2; EXP-PHYSICS-35402003775 handoff carry_forward)

K2 PMI = 0.933 bits and K3 PMI = 1.221 bits are reproducible point estimates (within rounding across 3+ experiments). Reproducibility is not the issue; interpretability is. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit.json V1)

Bootstrap CI for K3-K2 includes zero [-0.275, 0.080] and bootstrap mean (-0.109) is not centered on observed (0.287), indicating K3 estimator fragility under session resampling due to action-history strata fragmentation (821 total, 510 used). (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit.json V4)
Positive control validates PMI pipeline on fully deterministic SPA: K3 PMI = 1.806 >= 1.0, p = 0.001. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 result.json:controls.C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL)

K1 (1.531) > K2 (0.933) on this SPA: marginal action predictability exceeds state-conditioned predictability due to coarse vs fine strata weighting, not information content inversion. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit.json V8)
Fragment-stripping destroys all state information: normalized PMI = 0.0 bits on TodoMVC. (EXP-PHYSICS-35290611436, EXP-PHYSICS-35308806126)

SPA environment has beyond-Markov structure by construction: choose_next(current,action,prev1,prev2) depends on 2-step history, so a valid estimator SHOULD detect K3>K2. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit.json V9)

Whether the 0.287-bit K3-K2 point estimate contains any real beyond-Markov signal or is entirely estimator artifact; cannot be distinguished until bias-corrected re-run.
Root cause of K3 bootstrap instability: strata fragmentation vs trajectory correlation vs estimator nonlinearity.
Asymptotic behavior at larger N (N=100000+): does K2 PMI plateau after 1.779 or continue growing? What is the limit?
Why K1 > K2 (marginal > state-conditioned PMI) and whether this inversion is property of hash-routed SPA or purely estimator weighting artifact.

do_not_assume: C-WEB-DYNAMICS is globally false. The 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal is real and reproducible. The MEASUREMENT_INVALID verdict is due to estimator non-convergence, not absence of signal.
Null bias is evidence against beyond-Markov signal. The permutation bias is intrinsic to PMI weighted averaging; it prevents interpretation but does not falsify the underlying dynamics.
All PMI null frameworks are exhausted. Truly orthogonal frameworks (Bayesian model comparison, likelihood ratio tests, non-PMI information-theoretic quantities) are untested.
The 0.933-bit K2 PMI demonstrates beyond-Markov dynamics in the C-WEB-DYNAMICS sense. The test is I(url_after; action | url_before, prev1, prev2) without history-conditioned baseline comparison.
Production SPA results generalize from this simulation. The 12-state SPA has 12 states, 4 deterministic candidates, hash-based selection, no anti-bot/auth/visual complexity.
The bias floor of ~0.41 bits at N=5000 is irreducible. Alternative estimators or different SPA designs may reduce or eliminate it.
K3-K2 difference of 0.287 bits reflects genuine beyond-Markov signal. Bootstrap instability (mean -0.109, CI includes zero) indicates the estimate is unreliable.

Phase 2 production testing was precluded by infrastructure. It was precluded by Phase 1 methodology falsification (estimator non-convergence); production testing requires valid estimator before being interpretable.

recommended_action: Design an estimator-revision experiment: develop and validate a bias-corrected conditional mutual information estimator (equal-weight PMI across strata, median PMI, or direct CMI via KSG/KNN) that converges as N increases. Apply to same 12-state hash-routed SPA (SEED=42) at N=5000 and N=50000. Decision rule: if corrected estimator's null control |mean| < 0.1 AND K3-K2 > 0.1 with bootstrap CI lower > 0.0, the beyond-Markov question is answered. If null control still fails, the problem is environment-level (deterministic strata mixing) not estimator-level, and SPA redesign is needed. If corrected K3-K2 <= 0.1 or CI includes 0, the signal is Markov. This is the minimum prerequisite before any further PMI-based claims on this SPA class.
